fixed8_advantage_analysis.physical_mechanism: Under high friction (mu_s = 0.75), the tactile estimator correctly observed low contact risk and selected a gentle 5.0 N initial preload to minimize object damage and force exposure. Under standard shear ramps and micro-probes, 5.0 N was 100% stable. However, when an adversarial fast ramp (v = 8.0 mm/s) occurred, microscopic breakaway occurred in < 5 ms, before the 50 N/s rate-limited gripper could ramp from 5 N to 12 N. Fixed 8N was already at 8.0 N prior to disturbance onset, providing enough normal capacity (0.75 * 8 = 6.0 N) to arrest the fast ramp without relying on actuation response. Because pre-touch probing cannot predict future task disturbances, Fixed 8N achieved higher aggregate success.

observability_limitations.finding: Static friction coefficient is weakly observable in linear elastic core (c/a >= 0.99). Epistemic uncertainty fallback is essential.
